In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah Al-ʿAṣr

It is Makki.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the dahr (time, the ages), and in it is a lesson, in the passing of the night and the day, that they follow one fixed order.

And it is reported from al-Hasan and Qatadah that it is al-ʿashiy (the late afternoon/evening).

The poet said:

(We set out with you in the morning, and the afternoon has grown short, and in the first setting out is the reward and the recompense.)

Al-ʿAṣrān are the night and the day, and it is said: they are the morning (al-ghadah) and the evening (al-ʿashiy).

Muqatil said: al-ʿAṣr is the prayer of ʿAṣr (al-ʿAṣr prayer).

And it is reported from some of them that it is the era of the Prophet (ﷺ), by which He swore. It is related that in the reading of ʿAli it is: "By the era and the calamities of time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds..." and it is in it until the end of life.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: "By the Lord of the ʿAṣr."

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss.﴾ Its meaning is: in deprivation (ghabn). It is said: in evil, and it is said: in destruction. Al-khusran (loss) is the loss of capital, and the capital of the human being is his life and his self; so when he disbelieves, his capital has gone. "Al-insan" is the disbeliever. It is said: it is singular in meaning but plural. It is said: it refers to a specific disbeliever: it is said he was Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and it is said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and it is said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 103, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who have believed and done righteous deeds﴾ means: through acts of obedience.

And His saying: ﴿and advised one another to truth﴾ al-Hasan and Qatadah said: that is, with the Qur'an and following it. It was also said: with monotheism (tawhid).

And from al-Suddi, regarding "bi-Allah": that is, they advised one another regarding Allah. And from al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad, who said: they urge one another to obey Allah.

And His saying: ﴿and advised one another to patience﴾ means patience concerning the disobedience (of Allah). It was also said: patience upon obedience. And a strange report (khabar gharib) has come through the narration of Abu Umamah that His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ refers to Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.

And His saying: ﴿Except those who have believed﴾ refers to Abu Bakr, ﴿and done righteous deeds﴾ refers to 'Umar, ﴿and advised one another to truth﴾ refers to 'Uthman, ﴿and advised one another to patience﴾ refers to 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them all.
